messages:
maria: seeing 502/504 spikes from edge services in us-west-2 starting ~09:12 UTC, correlated with a huge fanout of model pulls to s3 during a bulk deploy. not an application error, looks like outbound port exhaustion on the NATGW :frowning: 
alex: confirmed from VPC flow logs — ephemeral ports hitting 64k limit on several NAT gateways. lots of ephemeral:src ports in TIME_WAIT.
sam: runbook idea: add an egress proxy pool in each AZ and multiplex model pulls to reduce connection churn. we tried this briefly in a dev cage and it cut sockets by ~6x.
jordan: what's the fastest mitigation to relieve current traffic? can we flip traffic to a different NATGW or scale up?
maria: we have two options short-term: 1) detach problem subnets and attach to another NAT (manual) or 2) switch to NAT instances with larger port range (slower to provision). leaning to temporary egress-proxy route to avoid infra churn.
oncall: deploy bot scheduled a replacement NATGW in us-west-2a at 09:30 UTC — provisioning now, ETA ~7 min.
infra-bot: aws-natgw-create started (request id: xxxxx-uw2a)
alex: while provisioning, can we enable keepalive on the model fetch clients? adding `Connection: keep-alive` and a longer tcp_keepalive reduces new ports. small config change in model-fetcher startup: 
```
HTTP_KEEPALIVE=true
TCP_KEEPIDLE=120
TCP_KEEPINTVL=30
```
maria: good call. pushing a config patch to canary model-pull service now. doing gradual roll.
sam: parallel step: enable S3 VPC Endpoint for the affected subnets so model pulls don't egress through NAT. that will cut a lot of the volume instantly if models are served from S3.
jordan: are model artifacts all in S3? we have some in external buckets in partner accounts.
alex: most are in s3-redwood-prod in our account but some partner fetches go to external URLs. for those we need proxy fallback.
maria: rolling out a sidecar proxy (s3-multiplex-proxy) to the model-puller DaemonSet. config excerpt: 
```yaml
proxy:
  max_connections: 1000
  keepalive_timeout: 60s
  pool_size: 50
```
sam: that sidecar reduces connection churn by pooling and reusing upstream connections. also adds caching for repeated pulls.
oncall: us-west-2a NATGW active, but we still see high TIME_WAIT counts — old sockets are draining.
jordan: longer-term: implement connection reuse library in the runtime (python requests with session pools + urllib3 keepalive) and have model fetchers stagger pulls during deploys. also gate large-scale pulls with a token bucket.
alex: also consider using ENI trunking / more secondary IPs per ENI to increase NAT capacity per AZ, or split workloads across more AZs.
maria: Action items: 
- alex: keepalive patch roll to all model-pull replicas (in progress)
- sam: test sidecar in canary and report socket reduction numbers (due today EOD)
- jordan: draft deploy-gating PR to throttle bulk pulls (WIP)
- infra: evaluate switching some traffic to NAT instances if AWS limits block us (infra ticket #2456)

jordan: assigning to ops rotation for follow-up, will update status page if user-facing errors persist.

alex: quick diagnostic commands we ran: 
```bash
# count TIME_WAIT by NAT gw
aws ec2 describe-network-interfaces --filters Name=availability-zone,Values=us-west-2a | jq '.NetworkInterfaces[] | .Description'
sudo ss -s | grep TIME-WAIT
netstat -an | awk '/:443/ {print $6}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head
```
maria: result summary: after keepalive canary and S3 endpoint attach, error rate dropped ~80% and ephemeral port usage is trending down. still watching for partner external pulls.
sam: let's add an automated alert rule: when ephemeral ports used > 70% for 5m, create a paged incident and kick off an auto-scaling NAT playbook.
oncall: alert created (rule id: ENG-INFRA-EGRESS-01)
jordan: small follow-up: consider pre-warming caches on Dedicated GPU nodes so they don't all pull same model simultaneously on cold start. that will reduce bursty egress during scale-ups.
maria: agreed — adding prefetch + local artifact mirror to Dedicated onboarding checklist.
alex: final note: document mitigation steps in the NATGW playbook and tag in runbook for future incidents. I'll open a PR to runbook repo.
maria: thanks everyone. will keep thread updated if anything new. :thumbsup:
